Banana_Black_Pitting_or_Banana_Rust.symptoms: Small dark or rusty brown spots/pitting on banana fruit surface; blemishes may reduce market value.
Banana_Black_Pitting_or_Banana_Rust.cause: Usually associated with fungal infection or rind/fruit spotting complexes under humid conditions.
Banana_Black_Pitting_or_Banana_Rust.organic_treatment: Remove infected plant debris, improve air movement, avoid fruit injury, and maintain field sanitation.
Banana_Black_Pitting_or_Banana_Rust.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended protective fungicide only after confirmation by an extension expert.
Banana_Black_Pitting_or_Banana_Rust.prevention: Use clean planting material, bag bunches where practiced, reduce mechanical injury, and manage humidity through spacing.
Banana_Black_Pitting_or_Banana_Rust.display_name: Banana Black Pitting Or Banana Rust

Banana_Crown_Rot.symptoms: Soft dark rot starting at the crown after harvest; fingers detach easily and fungal growth may appear.
Banana_Crown_Rot.cause: Post-harvest fungal complex commonly involving Colletotrichum, Fusarium, Lasiodiplodia and related fungi.
Banana_Crown_Rot.organic_treatment: Harvest carefully, avoid injuries, sanitize knives and packing surfaces, remove decayed hands, and keep fruit dry.
Banana_Crown_Rot.chemical_treatment: Post-harvest fungicide treatment may be used where locally approved and recommended.
Banana_Crown_Rot.prevention: Use clean handling practices, rapid cooling/ventilation, avoid crown damage, and maintain packing-house sanitation.

Banana_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Banana_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Banana_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Banana_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Banana_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Banana_fungal_disease.symptoms: Leaf spots, yellowing, necrotic streaks or blotches depending on the fungal pathogen involved.
Banana_fungal_disease.cause: Unspecified fungal disease; common banana foliar fungi are favored by high humidity and dense canopy.
Banana_fungal_disease.organic_treatment: Remove heavily infected leaves, improve drainage and spacing, and maintain field sanitation.
Banana_fungal_disease.chemical_treatment: Apply locally recommended fungicide only after disease identification.
Banana_fungal_disease.prevention: Use disease-free suckers/tissue culture plants, improve airflow, and avoid overhead irrigation where possible.

Banana_leaf_Banana_Scab_Moth.symptoms: Scarring, corky patches or superficial damage on developing fruits/leaves; larvae may feed under bracts.
Banana_leaf_Banana_Scab_Moth.cause: Insect pest damage caused by banana scab moth larvae.
Banana_leaf_Banana_Scab_Moth.organic_treatment: Remove old bracts and trash, maintain field sanitation, and bag bunches where recommended.
Banana_leaf_Banana_Scab_Moth.chemical_treatment: Use locally approved insecticide only if pest pressure is high and after expert advice.
Banana_leaf_Banana_Scab_Moth.prevention: Regular field monitoring, bunch covering, sanitation, and removal of infested material.

Banana_leaf_Black_Sigatoka.symptoms: Dark brown to black streaks and elongated leaf spots; severe infection causes leaf drying and reduced bunch filling.
Banana_leaf_Black_Sigatoka.cause: Fungal leaf spot disease caused by Pseudocercospora fijiensis.
Banana_leaf_Black_Sigatoka.organic_treatment: Remove severely infected leaves, improve airflow, reduce shade, and maintain plantation sanitation.
Banana_leaf_Black_Sigatoka.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide rotation where disease pressure is high; follow local extension guidance.
Banana_leaf_Black_Sigatoka.prevention: Plant tolerant varieties where available, avoid dense canopy, improve drainage, and monitor during humid weather.

Banana_leaf_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Banana_leaf_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Banana_leaf_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Banana_leaf_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Banana_leaf_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Banana_leaf__Black_Leaf_Streak.symptoms: Narrow reddish-brown streaks that enlarge into dark necrotic lesions; leaves may dry prematurely.
Banana_leaf__Black_Leaf_Streak.cause: Fungal disease; commonly known as black leaf streak/black Sigatoka caused by Pseudocercospora fijiensis.
Banana_leaf__Black_Leaf_Streak.organic_treatment: Prune infected leaves, improve ventilation, and remove diseased plant debris.
Banana_leaf__Black_Leaf_Streak.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended fungicide programmes where necessary.
Banana_leaf__Black_Leaf_Streak.prevention: Use clean planting material, resistant/tolerant varieties where available, good spacing, and field sanitation.

Banana_leaf__Panama_Disease..symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of older leaves, splitting of pseudostem, vascular browning inside the plant.
Banana_leaf__Panama_Disease..cause: Fusarium wilt caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense.
Banana_leaf__Panama_Disease..organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants, avoid moving contaminated soil, and improve drainage.
Banana_leaf__Panama_Disease..chemical_treatment: No reliable curative chemical treatment for infected plants; soil treatment options must be guided locally.
Banana_leaf__Panama_Disease..prevention: Use disease-free planting material, resistant varieties where available, farm hygiene, and avoid planting in infested soil.

Cauliflower_Bacterial_spot_rot.symptoms: Water-soaked spots or soft rotting on curds/leaves; affected tissue may become slimy and foul smelling.
Cauliflower_Bacterial_spot_rot.cause: Bacterial infection, often favored by wet conditions and wounds.
Cauliflower_Bacterial_spot_rot.organic_treatment: Remove infected plants, avoid overhead irrigation, improve field drainage, and maintain sanitation.
Cauliflower_Bacterial_spot_rot.chemical_treatment: Copper-based bactericides may reduce spread if locally recommended; antibiotics should not be used without official guidance.
Cauliflower_Bacterial_spot_rot.prevention: Use clean seed/seedlings, crop rotation, avoid working in wet fields, and control injuries.

Cauliflower_Black_Rot.symptoms: V-shaped yellow lesions from leaf margins, blackened veins, stunting and curd quality loss.
Cauliflower_Black_Rot.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris.
Cauliflower_Black_Rot.organic_treatment: Remove infected residues, rotate with non-crucifer crops, and avoid overhead irrigation.
Cauliflower_Black_Rot.chemical_treatment: Copper sprays may help reduce spread where recommended, but sanitation and seed health are primary.
Cauliflower_Black_Rot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed, hot-water seed treatment where recommended, crop rotation, and field sanitation.

Cauliflower_Downy_Mildew.symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaf surface with grey-white downy growth underneath; young plants may be stunted.
Cauliflower_Downy_Mildew.cause: Oomycete disease commonly caused by Hyaloperonospora/Peronospora species under cool humid conditions.
Cauliflower_Downy_Mildew.organic_treatment: Improve airflow, avoid overcrowding, remove infected debris, and irrigate early in the day.
Cauliflower_Downy_Mildew.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide for downy mildew if disease pressure is high.
Cauliflower_Downy_Mildew.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, crop rotation, nursery hygiene, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

Cauliflower_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Cauliflower_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Cauliflower_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Cauliflower_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Cauliflower_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Corn_Blight.symptoms: Elongated tan to brown lesions on leaves; severe infection causes large blighted areas and premature drying.
Corn_Blight.cause: Fungal leaf blight, commonly caused by Exserohilum turcicum or related pathogens depending on region.
Corn_Blight.organic_treatment: Destroy infected residues, rotate crops, and use balanced nutrition.
Corn_Blight.chemical_treatment: Apply recommended fungicide if disease appears early and weather favors spread.
Corn_Blight.prevention: Use resistant hybrids, crop rotation, residue management, and avoid dense planting.

Corn_Common_Rust.symptoms: Small cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces; pustules may turn dark later.
Corn_Common_Rust.cause: Fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi.
Corn_Common_Rust.organic_treatment: Use resistant varieties and remove volunteer maize where practical.
Corn_Common_Rust.chemical_treatment: Fungicide may be justified in susceptible hybrids under severe early infection.
Corn_Common_Rust.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, monitor during cool humid weather, and avoid late planting where rust is common.

Corn_Gray_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Rectangular grey to tan lesions limited by leaf veins; severe cases cause leaf blighting.
Corn_Gray_Leaf_Spot.cause: Fungal disease caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis and related species.
Corn_Gray_Leaf_Spot.organic_treatment: Crop rotation and residue management to reduce inoculum.
Corn_Gray_Leaf_Spot.chemical_treatment: Use fungicides only when disease risk and crop stage justify it locally.
Corn_Gray_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Use resistant hybrids, rotate away from maize, manage residue, and improve field airflow.

Corn_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Corn_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Corn_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Corn_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Corn_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Cotton_Aphids.symptoms: Clusters of small soft-bodied insects on tender leaves; curling, yellowing, sticky honeydew and sooty mould may occur.
Cotton_Aphids.cause: Sap-feeding insect pest, commonly Aphis gossypii.
Cotton_Aphids.organic_treatment: Conserve natural enemies, wash off small colonies, remove weeds, and use neem-based products where suitable.
Cotton_Aphids.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended selective insecticide only when economic threshold is crossed.
Cotton_Aphids.prevention: Regular scouting, avoid excessive nitrogen, conserve ladybird beetles/lacewings, and manage weeds.

Cotton_Army worm.symptoms: Irregular holes in leaves, defoliation, cut seedlings or damaged squares/bolls depending on species and stage.
Cotton_Army worm.cause: Larvae of armyworm moths, commonly Spodoptera species.
Cotton_Army worm.organic_treatment: Handpick larvae in small plots, use pheromone traps, conserve natural enemies, and apply biopesticides such as Bt where suitable.
Cotton_Army worm.chemical_treatment: Use recommended insecticide only at threshold level and rotate modes of action.
Cotton_Army worm.prevention: Monitor egg masses/young larvae, destroy crop residues, manage weeds, and avoid indiscriminate sprays.

Cotton_Bacterial blight.symptoms: Angular water-soaked leaf spots, dark lesions along veins, black arm symptoms on stems, and boll lesions.
Cotton_Bacterial blight.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum.
Cotton_Bacterial blight.organic_treatment: Use disease-free seed, remove infected residues, rotate crops, and avoid overhead irrigation.
Cotton_Bacterial blight.chemical_treatment: Copper-based sprays may help reduce spread in some situations if locally recommended.
Cotton_Bacterial blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, acid-delinted/certified seed, crop rotation, sanitation, and avoid working in wet fields.

Cotton_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Cotton_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Cotton_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Cotton_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Cotton_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Guava_fruit_Anthracnose.symptoms: Sunken dark circular spots on fruit, often with pinkish spore masses; fruit rot may develop.
Guava_fruit_Anthracnose.cause: Fungal disease commonly caused by Colletotrichum species.
Guava_fruit_Anthracnose.organic_treatment: Remove infected fruits, prune for airflow, avoid fruit injury, and maintain orchard sanitation.
Guava_fruit_Anthracnose.chemical_treatment: Use recommended protective fungicide during high-risk wet periods if advised locally.
Guava_fruit_Anthracnose.prevention: Field sanitation, pruning, bagging fruits where feasible, and careful harvesting.

Guava_fruit_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Guava_fruit_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Guava_fruit_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Guava_fruit_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Guava_fruit_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Guava_fruit_Scab.symptoms: Corky scabby lesions on fruit surface; fruit may be distorted or blemished.
Guava_fruit_Scab.cause: Fungal disease often associated with Elsinoë/Sphaceloma species or scab-like fungal complexes.
Guava_fruit_Scab.organic_treatment: Remove infected fruits and plant debris, prune for airflow, and avoid overhead wetting.
Guava_fruit_Scab.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended fungicide if disease is recurrent.
Guava_fruit_Scab.prevention: Sanitation, pruning, use healthy planting material, and protect young fruits during wet weather.

Guava_fruit_Styler_end_root.symptoms: Rotting near stylar/blossom end of fruit; affected tissue turns brown to black and may become sunken.
Guava_fruit_Styler_end_root.cause: Likely stylar-end fruit rot caused by fungal infection; exact pathogen may vary.
Guava_fruit_Styler_end_root.organic_treatment: Remove infected fruits, avoid injuries, improve orchard hygiene, and harvest carefully.
Guava_fruit_Styler_end_root.chemical_treatment: Use only locally recommended post-harvest or field fungicide after confirmation.
Guava_fruit_Styler_end_root.prevention: Sanitation, fruit bagging where feasible, balanced nutrition, and careful post-harvest handling.

Guava_leaf_Anthracnose.symptoms: Dark necrotic spots on leaves; young shoots may show dieback under severe infection.
Guava_leaf_Anthracnose.cause: Fungal disease commonly caused by Colletotrichum species.
Guava_leaf_Anthracnose.organic_treatment: Prune infected twigs, remove fallen leaves, and improve canopy ventilation.
Guava_leaf_Anthracnose.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide during humid periods if necessary.
Guava_leaf_Anthracnose.prevention: Orchard sanitation, pruning, avoid overhead irrigation, and use healthy planting material.

Guava_leaf_Canker.symptoms: Corky or necrotic lesions on leaves/twigs; cracking or canker-like symptoms may occur.
Guava_leaf_Canker.cause: May be caused by fungal or bacterial pathogens; exact cause requires local diagnosis.
Guava_leaf_Canker.organic_treatment: Prune and destroy infected twigs, disinfect pruning tools, and reduce plant stress.
Guava_leaf_Canker.chemical_treatment: Apply locally recommended protectant only after pathogen confirmation.
Guava_leaf_Canker.prevention: Use healthy planting material, avoid injuries, maintain tree vigor, and sanitize tools.

Guava_leaf_Dot.symptoms: Small dot-like leaf spots, often brown/black; heavy infection can cause yellowing or premature leaf fall.
Guava_leaf_Dot.cause: Likely fungal leaf spot complex; exact pathogen may vary.
Guava_leaf_Dot.organic_treatment: Remove infected leaves and improve canopy airflow.
Guava_leaf_Dot.chemical_treatment: Use a recommended protective fungicide if disease is severe.
Guava_leaf_Dot.prevention: Sanitation, pruning, balanced nutrition, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

Guava_leaf_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Guava_leaf_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Guava_leaf_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Guava_leaf_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Guava_leaf_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Guava_leaf_Rust.symptoms: Rusty orange-brown pustules or spots on leaves; infected leaves may yellow or drop.
Guava_leaf_Rust.organic_treatment: Remove infected leaves, improve airflow, and maintain sanitation.
Guava_leaf_Rust.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended fungicide if severe or recurring.
Guava_leaf_Rust.prevention: Avoid dense canopy, remove alternate hosts if known, and monitor during humid weather.

Jute_Cescospora Leaf Spot.symptoms: Small brown to grey leaf spots with darker margins; spots may coalesce and cause leaf drying.
Jute_Cescospora Leaf Spot.cause: Fungal leaf spot caused by Cercospora species.
Jute_Cescospora Leaf Spot.organic_treatment: Remove infected residues, rotate crops, and avoid dense planting.
Jute_Cescospora Leaf Spot.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide if severe and locally advised.
Jute_Cescospora Leaf Spot.prevention: Use clean seed, crop rotation, field sanitation, and balanced fertilization.

Jute_Golden Mosaic.symptoms: Yellow/golden mosaic patches on leaves, leaf curling, stunting and reduced fibre yield.
Jute_Golden Mosaic.cause: Viral disease generally associated with begomovirus infection transmitted by whiteflies.
Jute_Golden Mosaic.organic_treatment: Remove infected plants early and manage weeds/alternate hosts.
Jute_Golden Mosaic.chemical_treatment: No curative chemical treatment for virus; manage whitefly vector using locally recommended measures.
Jute_Golden Mosaic.prevention: Use tolerant varieties where available, healthy seed, rogue infected plants, and control whiteflies.

Jute_Healthy Leaf.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Jute_Healthy Leaf.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Jute_Healthy Leaf.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Jute_Healthy Leaf.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Jute_Healthy Leaf.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Mango_Anthracnose.symptoms: Black sunken spots on leaves, flowers or fruits; blossom blight and fruit rot may occur.
Mango_Anthracnose.cause: Fungal disease caused by Colletotrichum species.
Mango_Anthracnose.organic_treatment: Prune infected twigs, remove mummified fruits, improve airflow, and maintain orchard sanitation.
Mango_Anthracnose.chemical_treatment: Use recommended protective fungicide during flowering/fruiting in wet conditions.
Mango_Anthracnose.prevention: Canopy pruning, sanitation, avoid overhead irrigation, and timely protection during humid weather.
Mango_Anthracnose.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Mango_Bacterial_Canker.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves, black cankers on twigs/stems, fruit spots and gummosis may occur.
Mango_Bacterial_Canker.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas species.
Mango_Bacterial_Canker.organic_treatment: Prune infected twigs, destroy infected material, and disinfect tools.
Mango_Bacterial_Canker.chemical_treatment: Copper-based bactericides may reduce spread where locally recommended.
Mango_Bacterial_Canker.prevention: Use healthy planting material, windbreaks to reduce injury, sanitation, and avoid overhead irrigation.
Mango_Bacterial_Canker.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Mango_Cutting_Weevil.symptoms: Cut marks, damaged shoots/leaves or feeding injury; affected young growth may dry or deform.
Mango_Cutting_Weevil.cause: Insect pest/weevil damage; exact species should be confirmed locally.
Mango_Cutting_Weevil.organic_treatment: Collect and destroy affected plant parts; maintain orchard sanitation.
Mango_Cutting_Weevil.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended insecticide only after pest identification and threshold assessment.
Mango_Cutting_Weevil.prevention: Regular scouting, sanitation, pruning of infested shoots, and avoiding neglected orchards.

Mango_Gall_Midge.symptoms: Small galls/blisters or raised spots on leaves/inflorescences; affected tissues may dry or drop.
Mango_Gall_Midge.cause: Insect pest caused by gall midge larvae feeding within plant tissues.
Mango_Gall_Midge.organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infested leaves/panicles; improve orchard sanitation.
Mango_Gall_Midge.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended insecticide if severe and timed to adult emergence.
Mango_Gall_Midge.prevention: Monitor new flush/panicles, collect fallen leaves, and maintain orchard hygiene.

Mango_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Mango_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Mango_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Mango_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Mango_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Mango_Powdery_Mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on flowers, young leaves and fruits; infected flowers may dry and drop.
Mango_Powdery_Mildew.cause: Fungal disease caused by Oidium/Erysiphe species.
Mango_Powdery_Mildew.organic_treatment: Prune dense canopy and remove infected panicles where practical.
Mango_Powdery_Mildew.chemical_treatment: Apply recommended sulphur or systemic fungicide as per local advisory during flowering.
Mango_Powdery_Mildew.prevention: Improve airflow, avoid excessive shade, monitor during cool dry-to-humid periods, and protect panicles early.
Mango_Powdery_Mildew.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Mango_Sooty_Mould.symptoms: Black sooty coating on leaves/fruits, usually on honeydew deposits; photosynthesis and fruit quality reduced.
Mango_Sooty_Mould.cause: Fungal growth on honeydew produced by sap-sucking insects such as scales, mealybugs or hoppers.
Mango_Sooty_Mould.organic_treatment: Wash leaves where feasible and manage honeydew-producing insects with neem/biocontrols.
Mango_Sooty_Mould.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended insecticide only if vector/pest population is high.
Mango_Sooty_Mould.prevention: Control sap-sucking pests, prune for airflow, and avoid excessive nitrogen.

Mango_die_back.symptoms: Drying of twigs from tips downward, leaf shedding, cankers and sometimes gummosis.
Mango_die_back.cause: Often caused by fungal pathogens such as Lasiodiplodia/Botryodiplodia species, favored by stress and wounds.
Mango_die_back.organic_treatment: Prune below infected portion, destroy prunings, disinfect tools, and improve tree vigor.
Mango_die_back.chemical_treatment: Apply recommended wound protectant/fungicide after pruning if advised locally.
Mango_die_back.prevention: Avoid pruning injuries during wet weather, maintain nutrition and irrigation, and remove dead wood.
Mango_die_back.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Papaya_Anthracnose.symptoms: Sunken circular dark spots on fruit, sometimes with pink/orange spore masses; leaf or stem spots may occur.
Papaya_Anthracnose.cause: Fungal disease caused by Colletotrichum species.
Papaya_Anthracnose.organic_treatment: Remove infected fruits, avoid injuries, maintain sanitation, and improve ventilation.
Papaya_Anthracnose.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide during wet periods or post-harvest treatment where approved.
Papaya_Anthracnose.prevention: Use clean planting material, field sanitation, careful harvesting, and avoid prolonged fruit wetness.

Papaya_BacterialSpot.symptoms: Water-soaked leaf or fruit spots that turn brown/black; lesions may be angular on leaves.
Papaya_BacterialSpot.cause: Bacterial leaf/fruit spot; exact pathogen should be confirmed locally.
Papaya_BacterialSpot.organic_treatment: Remove infected plant parts, avoid overhead irrigation, and sanitize tools.
Papaya_BacterialSpot.chemical_treatment: Copper-based sprays may reduce spread where locally recommended.
Papaya_BacterialSpot.prevention: Use clean seedlings, avoid working in wet fields, improve spacing and airflow.

Papaya_Curl.symptoms: Leaves curl, crinkle, thicken or become distorted; plant may be stunted with reduced fruiting.
Papaya_Curl.cause: Viral disease commonly associated with leaf curl virus transmitted by whiteflies.
Papaya_Curl.organic_treatment: Rogue infected plants early and remove weed hosts.
Papaya_Curl.chemical_treatment: No curative chemical treatment for virus; manage whitefly vector with locally recommended methods.
Papaya_Curl.prevention: Raise seedlings under insect-proof conditions, use healthy seedlings, barrier crops, and whitefly monitoring.

Papaya_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Papaya_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Papaya_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Papaya_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Papaya_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Papaya_Mealybug.symptoms: White cottony insect colonies on leaves, stems and fruits; yellowing, stunting, honeydew and sooty mould may occur.
Papaya_Mealybug.cause: Sap-sucking insect pest, commonly Paracoccus marginatus or related mealybugs.
Papaya_Mealybug.organic_treatment: Conserve parasitoids/predators, prune infested parts, wash colonies, and use neem-based products if suitable.
Papaya_Mealybug.chemical_treatment: Use selective insecticide only if severe and locally recommended.
Papaya_Mealybug.prevention: Regular scouting, control ants, remove weeds, and avoid movement of infested material.

Papaya_Mite_disease.symptoms: Yellow speckling, bronzing, leaf curling or webbing; severe infestation causes leaf drying and fruit blemish.
Papaya_Mite_disease.cause: Mite infestation, often spider mites/broad mites depending on symptoms.
Papaya_Mite_disease.organic_treatment: Spray water to reduce dust, conserve predatory mites, remove heavily infested leaves, and use neem/horticultural oils where suitable.
Papaya_Mite_disease.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended miticide only after confirming mite species and threshold.
Papaya_Mite_disease.prevention: Avoid dusty conditions, monitor undersides of leaves, avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum insecticides.

Papaya_Mosaic.symptoms: Mosaic mottling, leaf distortion, stunting and reduced fruit quality.
Papaya_Mosaic.cause: Viral disease; commonly transmitted mechanically or by insect vectors depending on virus.
Papaya_Mosaic.organic_treatment: Remove infected plants and control weed hosts.
Papaya_Mosaic.chemical_treatment: No curative chemical treatment; manage vectors where relevant using local recommendations.
Papaya_Mosaic.prevention: Use healthy seedlings, rogue infected plants, control vectors/weeds, and sanitize tools.

Papaya_Ringspot.symptoms: Mosaic and shoestring leaves, oily streaks on stems/petioles, ring spots on fruits and plant stunting.
Papaya_Ringspot.cause: Papaya ringspot virus, commonly transmitted by aphids.
Papaya_Ringspot.organic_treatment: Rogue infected plants early, remove cucurbit/weed hosts nearby, and use barrier crops.
Papaya_Ringspot.chemical_treatment: No curative chemical treatment for virus; vector management may reduce spread but is not fully effective.
Papaya_Ringspot.prevention: Use disease-free seedlings, insect-proof nursery, barrier crops such as maize/sorghum, and resistant/tolerant varieties where available.

Potato_Black_Scurf.symptoms: Black hard scurf-like bodies on tuber surface; stem cankers, poor emergence and stolon pruning may occur.
Potato_Black_Scurf.cause: Fungal disease caused by Rhizoctonia solani.
Potato_Black_Scurf.organic_treatment: Use clean seed tubers, rotate crops, improve drainage, and avoid planting in cold wet soil.
Potato_Black_Scurf.chemical_treatment: Seed treatment fungicide may be used where locally recommended.
Potato_Black_Scurf.prevention: Certified seed, crop rotation, sanitation, proper planting depth and soil conditions.

Potato_Blackleg.symptoms: Black decay at stem base, yellowing, wilting, and soft watery tuber rot.
Potato_Blackleg.cause: Bacterial disease commonly caused by Pectobacterium/Dickeya species.
Potato_Blackleg.organic_treatment: Use certified seed, remove infected plants, avoid excessive irrigation, and improve drainage.
Potato_Blackleg.chemical_treatment: Chemical control is limited; use only locally advised seed treatment or sanitation measures.
Potato_Blackleg.prevention: Certified disease-free seed, avoid cutting/handling injuries, good storage ventilation, and field sanitation.

Potato_Blackspot_Bruising.symptoms: Dark grey/black internal spots under the skin after impact; no external rot initially.
Potato_Blackspot_Bruising.cause: Physiological bruise caused by mechanical impact, low tuber hydration, or handling stress; not a pathogen.
Potato_Blackspot_Bruising.organic_treatment: Handle tubers gently and maintain proper storage humidity/temperature.
Potato_Blackspot_Bruising.prevention: Avoid rough harvesting, maintain soil moisture before harvest, reduce drops during handling, and cure tubers properly.

Potato_Brown_Rot.symptoms: Wilting plants; brown vascular ring in tubers with bacterial ooze; tubers may rot.
Potato_Brown_Rot.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Ralstonia solanacearum.
Potato_Brown_Rot.organic_treatment: Rogue infected plants, avoid contaminated irrigation water, rotate crops, and improve drainage.
Potato_Brown_Rot.chemical_treatment: No reliable curative chemical treatment; follow local quarantine and sanitation advice.
Potato_Brown_Rot.prevention: Use certified seed, avoid infested fields, rotate with non-hosts, and sanitize tools/equipment.

Potato_Common_Scab.symptoms: Rough corky raised or pitted lesions on tuber skin; market quality reduced.
Potato_Common_Scab.cause: Soil-borne bacterial disease caused by Streptomyces species.
Potato_Common_Scab.organic_treatment: Maintain soil moisture during tuber initiation and use organic matter/rotation practices.
Potato_Common_Scab.chemical_treatment: Chemical control is limited; use local seed/soil treatment recommendations only.
Potato_Common_Scab.prevention: Use certified seed, rotate crops, avoid alkaline soil conditions, and maintain moisture during tuber formation.

Potato_Dry_Rot.symptoms: Sunken wrinkled tuber lesions with dry internal rot; white/pink fungal growth may appear in storage.
Potato_Dry_Rot.cause: Fungal storage disease caused by Fusarium species.
Potato_Dry_Rot.organic_treatment: Avoid tuber injury, cure tubers before storage, remove infected tubers, and improve ventilation.
Potato_Dry_Rot.chemical_treatment: Use recommended seed treatment/storage fungicide only where approved.
Potato_Dry_Rot.prevention: Careful harvesting, sanitation, storage ventilation, curing, and use of healthy seed tubers.

Potato_Healthy_Potatoes.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Potato_Healthy_Potatoes.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Potato_Healthy_Potatoes.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Potato_Healthy_Potatoes.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Potato_Healthy_Potatoes.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Potato_Miscellaneous.symptoms: Unspecified potato disorder/disease class; symptoms need manual confirmation from image and field context.
Potato_Miscellaneous.organic_treatment: Isolate affected samples and compare with confirmed disease symptoms; maintain sanitation.
Potato_Miscellaneous.chemical_treatment: Do not apply chemical treatment until diagnosis is confirmed.
Potato_Miscellaneous.prevention: Use certified seed, crop rotation, good drainage and regular scouting.

Potato_Pink_Rot.symptoms: Tubers show watery rot and turn pink/salmon after cutting and exposure to air; usually starts near stolon end.
Potato_Pink_Rot.cause: Oomycete disease caused by Phytophthora erythroseptica.
Potato_Pink_Rot.organic_treatment: Improve drainage, avoid harvesting wet fields, remove infected tubers, and store properly.
Potato_Pink_Rot.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended fungicide/seed treatment where disease is known.
Potato_Pink_Rot.prevention: Avoid waterlogging, crop rotation, careful harvest, and storage hygiene.

Potato_Soft_Rot.symptoms: Soft watery foul-smelling tuber rot; tissue collapses rapidly especially in warm wet storage.
Potato_Soft_Rot.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Pectobacterium/Dickeya species.
Potato_Soft_Rot.organic_treatment: Remove infected tubers, avoid wounds, dry/cure tubers, and improve storage ventilation.
Potato_Soft_Rot.chemical_treatment: Chemical control is limited; sanitation and handling are most important.
Potato_Soft_Rot.prevention: Use healthy seed, avoid injury, disinfect equipment, harvest in dry conditions, and maintain cool ventilated storage.

Rice_Blast.symptoms: Diamond-shaped grey lesions with brown margins on leaves; neck blast can cause panicle breakage and empty grains.
Rice_Blast.cause: Fungal disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae.
Rice_Blast.organic_treatment: Use balanced nitrogen, remove infected residues, and maintain proper water management.
Rice_Blast.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide when disease risk is high, especially for neck blast protection.
Rice_Blast.prevention: Resistant varieties, balanced fertilization, seed treatment where advised, and monitoring during humid weather.
Rice_Blast.source: International Rice Research Institute / Rice Knowledge Bank

Rice_Brownspot.symptoms: Small circular to oval brown spots on leaves; grain discoloration may occur; often worse in nutrient-stressed fields.
Rice_Brownspot.cause: Fungal disease caused by Bipolaris oryzae.
Rice_Brownspot.organic_treatment: Improve soil fertility, use clean seed, and remove infected residues.
Rice_Brownspot.chemical_treatment: Seed treatment/fungicide may be used where recommended.
Rice_Brownspot.prevention: Balanced nutrition, resistant varieties, clean seed, and field sanitation.
Rice_Brownspot.source: International Rice Research Institute / Rice Knowledge Bank

Rice_Tungro.symptoms: Yellow-orange discoloration, stunting, reduced tillering and poor panicle development.
Rice_Tungro.cause: Viral disease complex transmitted by green leafhoppers.
Rice_Tungro.organic_treatment: Rogue infected plants and control volunteer rice/weeds.
Rice_Tungro.chemical_treatment: No cure for infected plants; manage leafhopper vectors using local IPM recommendations.
Rice_Tungro.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, synchronize planting, remove infected plants, and manage green leafhopper vectors.
Rice_Tungro.source: International Rice Research Institute / Rice Knowledge Bank

Rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked yellow lesions from leaf tips/margins that expand into straw-colored blight; kresek wilting in seedlings.
Rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae.
Rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.organic_treatment: Avoid clipping seedlings, use balanced nitrogen, improve drainage, and remove infected residues.
Rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.chemical_treatment: Chemical control is generally unreliable; use local copper/bactericide guidance only where recommended.
Rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.prevention: Resistant varieties, clean seed, field sanitation, balanced fertilizer, and avoid wounds during transplanting.
Rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.source: International Rice Research Institute / Rice Knowledge Bank

Rice_bacterial_leaf_streak.symptoms: Narrow water-soaked translucent streaks between veins that turn yellow-brown; bacterial ooze may appear.
Rice_bacterial_leaf_streak.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola.
Rice_bacterial_leaf_streak.organic_treatment: Avoid excessive nitrogen, improve field sanitation, and reduce leaf wetness.
Rice_bacterial_leaf_streak.chemical_treatment: Chemical control is limited; follow local advisory if bactericides are recommended.
Rice_bacterial_leaf_streak.prevention: Resistant varieties where available, clean seed, balanced fertilizer, and avoid dense planting.
Rice_bacterial_leaf_streak.source: International Rice Research Institute / Rice Knowledge Bank

Rice_bacterial_panicle_blight.symptoms: Poor grain filling, panicle discoloration and upright panicles; grains may be sterile or discolored.
Rice_bacterial_panicle_blight.cause: Bacterial disease commonly associated with Burkholderia glumae and related bacteria, favored by high temperature.
Rice_bacterial_panicle_blight.organic_treatment: Use clean seed, avoid excessive nitrogen, and remove infected residues.
Rice_bacterial_panicle_blight.chemical_treatment: No reliable curative treatment; seed treatment or bactericide use must follow local guidance.
Rice_bacterial_panicle_blight.prevention: Use tolerant varieties where available, clean seed, balanced fertilization, and avoid heat/water stress where possible.
Rice_bacterial_panicle_blight.source: International Rice Research Institute / Rice Knowledge Bank

Rice_dead_heart.symptoms: Central shoot dries and can be easily pulled out; dead heart in vegetative stage and whiteheads at reproductive stage.
Rice_dead_heart.cause: Usually caused by rice stem borer larvae feeding inside tillers.
Rice_dead_heart.organic_treatment: Remove egg masses, conserve natural enemies, and use pheromone/light traps where recommended.
Rice_dead_heart.chemical_treatment: Use recommended insecticide only when economic threshold is crossed.
Rice_dead_heart.prevention: Synchronous planting, stubble destruction, balanced nitrogen, and regular scouting.
Rice_dead_heart.source: International Rice Research Institute / Rice Knowledge Bank

Rice_downy_mildew.symptoms: Yellowing, chlorotic streaks, stunting and sometimes downy growth; symptoms vary by pathogen and region.
Rice_downy_mildew.cause: Oomycete disease; exact pathogen requires local confirmation.
Rice_downy_mildew.organic_treatment: Improve drainage, remove infected plants/residues, and avoid dense planting.
Rice_downy_mildew.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide only after confirmation.
Rice_downy_mildew.prevention: Use clean seed, resistant varieties where available, field sanitation and water management.
Rice_downy_mildew.source: International Rice Research Institute / Rice Knowledge Bank

Rice_hispa.symptoms: Scraped white streaks on leaves; adults and larvae feed on leaf tissue causing whitish patches and drying.
Rice_hispa.cause: Insect pest, rice hispa beetle Dicladispa armigera.
Rice_hispa.organic_treatment: Clip and destroy infested leaf tips, conserve natural enemies, and avoid excessive nitrogen.
Rice_hispa.chemical_treatment: Use recommended insecticide only if infestation exceeds threshold.
Rice_hispa.prevention: Regular scouting, balanced fertilizer, remove grassy weeds, and avoid staggered planting.
Rice_hispa.source: International Rice Research Institute / Rice Knowledge Bank

Rice_normal.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Rice_normal.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Rice_normal.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Rice_normal.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Rice_normal.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Sugarcane_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Sugarcane_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Sugarcane_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Sugarcane_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Sugarcane_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Sugarcane_Mosaic.symptoms: Mosaic pattern of light and dark green/yellow patches on leaves; stunting may occur.
Sugarcane_Mosaic.cause: Viral disease, commonly sugarcane mosaic virus complex, often transmitted by aphids or infected setts.
Sugarcane_Mosaic.organic_treatment: Rogue infected clumps and use healthy seed cane.
Sugarcane_Mosaic.chemical_treatment: No curative chemical treatment; manage aphid vectors only if needed.
Sugarcane_Mosaic.prevention: Use disease-free setts, resistant varieties, field sanitation, and remove infected clumps.

Sugarcane_RedRot.symptoms: Reddening of internal cane tissue with white patches, sour smell, drying of top leaves and cane death.
Sugarcane_RedRot.cause: Fungal disease caused by Colletotrichum falcatum.
Sugarcane_RedRot.organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected clumps, avoid ratooning diseased fields, and use healthy setts.
Sugarcane_RedRot.chemical_treatment: Sett treatment/fungicide may be used where locally recommended.
Sugarcane_RedRot.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, use disease-free seed cane, crop rotation, and field sanitation.

Sugarcane_Rust.symptoms: Orange to brown pustules on leaves; severe infection causes leaf drying and reduced growth.
Sugarcane_Rust.cause: Fungal rust disease caused by Puccinia species.
Sugarcane_Rust.organic_treatment: Use resistant varieties and remove heavily infected leaves where practical.
Sugarcane_Rust.chemical_treatment: Fungicide use may be considered for severe infection under local guidance.
Sugarcane_Rust.prevention: Resistant varieties, balanced nutrition, and monitoring during humid weather.

Sugarcane_Yellow.symptoms: Yellowing of midrib/leaves, reduced vigor and yield; symptoms may resemble nutrient stress.
Sugarcane_Yellow.cause: Often associated with sugarcane yellow leaf virus, but nutrient stress should be ruled out.
Sugarcane_Yellow.organic_treatment: Rogue infected plants and maintain crop vigor.
Sugarcane_Yellow.chemical_treatment: No curative chemical treatment for viral infection.
Sugarcane_Yellow.prevention: Use disease-free planting material, resistant varieties where available, vector management and balanced nutrition.

Tea_Anthracnose.symptoms: Brown necrotic leaf spots, often on young leaves; severe infection may cause blighting and leaf drop.
Tea_Anthracnose.cause: Fungal disease caused by Colletotrichum species.
Tea_Anthracnose.organic_treatment: Prune infected shoots, improve airflow, and remove diseased debris.
Tea_Anthracnose.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide if disease pressure is high.
Tea_Anthracnose.prevention: Good pruning, sanitation, shade management and avoiding prolonged leaf wetness.

Tea_algal_leaf.symptoms: Greenish, orange or reddish-brown raised spots on leaves; affected areas may become necrotic.
Tea_algal_leaf.cause: Algal disease commonly caused by Cephaleuros species.
Tea_algal_leaf.organic_treatment: Improve plant vigor, prune for airflow, and reduce shade/humidity.
Tea_algal_leaf.chemical_treatment: Copper-based sprays may be recommended in severe cases under local guidance.
Tea_algal_leaf.prevention: Balanced nutrition, shade regulation, pruning and field sanitation.

Tea_bird_eye_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with pale/grey center and dark border, resembling a bird's eye.
Tea_bird_eye_spot.cause: Fungal leaf spot disease; exact pathogen may vary by region.
Tea_bird_eye_spot.organic_treatment: Remove affected leaves during pruning and improve ventilation.
Tea_bird_eye_spot.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide if economically significant.
Tea_bird_eye_spot.prevention: Sanitation, shade regulation, pruning and monitoring in humid conditions.

Tea_brown_blight.symptoms: Brown leaf lesions that enlarge and coalesce; severe cases cause blighting and defoliation.
Tea_brown_blight.cause: Fungal disease often associated with Colletotrichum/Glomerella or related fungi.
Tea_brown_blight.organic_treatment: Prune diseased shoots, remove infected litter and improve canopy airflow.
Tea_brown_blight.chemical_treatment: Use locally recommended fungicide if severe.
Tea_brown_blight.prevention: Maintain bush health, proper shade, drainage and sanitation.

Tea_gray_light.symptoms: Greyish leaf spots or blighted patches; exact disease identity should be manually confirmed.
Tea_gray_light.cause: Unknown/ambiguous class label; may refer to a grey leaf spot/blight complex.
Tea_gray_light.organic_treatment: Remove infected leaves and improve air circulation.
Tea_gray_light.chemical_treatment: Do not apply chemical treatment until diagnosis is confirmed.
Tea_gray_light.prevention: Monitor symptoms, maintain sanitation, and verify with local tea disease guide.

Tea_healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Tea_healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Tea_healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Tea_healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Tea_healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Tea_red_leaf_spot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular to irregular leaf spots; severe infection may lead to leaf drop.
Tea_red_leaf_spot.cause: Likely fungal leaf spot disease; exact pathogen requires confirmation.
Tea_red_leaf_spot.organic_treatment: Remove infected leaves and improve drainage/airflow.
Tea_red_leaf_spot.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide only if severe and verified.
Tea_red_leaf_spot.prevention: Sanitation, pruning, shade management and regular monitoring.

Tea_white_spot.symptoms: White to pale spots on leaves, sometimes with necrotic margins; exact disease may vary.
Tea_white_spot.cause: Likely fungal leaf spot or physiological disorder; requires manual verification.
Tea_white_spot.organic_treatment: Improve bush vigor, remove infected leaves and reduce leaf wetness.
Tea_white_spot.chemical_treatment: Use chemical control only after confirmed diagnosis.
Tea_white_spot.prevention: Good pruning, balanced nutrition, sanitation and shade management.

Tomato_Bacterial_Spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn dark and may have yellow halos; scabby spots on fruit.
Tomato_Bacterial_Spot.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas species.
Tomato_Bacterial_Spot.organic_treatment: Use clean seed/transplants, remove infected debris, avoid overhead irrigation and working in wet plants.
Tomato_Bacterial_Spot.chemical_treatment: Copper-based bactericides may suppress spread where locally recommended.
Tomato_Bacterial_Spot.prevention: Certified seed, crop rotation, sanitation, drip irrigation and resistant varieties where available.

Tomato_Early_Blight.symptoms: Brown leaf spots with concentric rings, usually starting on lower leaves; defoliation and fruit lesions may occur.
Tomato_Early_Blight.cause: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani.
Tomato_Early_Blight.organic_treatment: Remove infected lower leaves, mulch to reduce soil splash, rotate crops and improve airflow.
Tomato_Early_Blight.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide if disease is spreading, especially in humid conditions.
Tomato_Early_Blight.prevention: Crop rotation, staking, sanitation, balanced nutrition and avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato_Late_Blight.symptoms: Large water-soaked grey-green lesions on leaves/stems; white mould may appear underside; fruit rot can occur.
Tomato_Late_Blight.cause: Oomycete disease caused by Phytophthora infestans.
Tomato_Late_Blight.organic_treatment: Destroy infected plants, avoid overhead irrigation and improve airflow.
Tomato_Late_Blight.chemical_treatment: Use recommended anti-oomycete fungicide urgently when disease risk is high.
Tomato_Late_Blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, disease-free seedlings, forecasting/weather monitoring and sanitation.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaves with olive-grey mould on undersides; leaves may curl and die.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.cause: Fungal disease caused by Passalora fulva, favored by high humidity.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.organic_treatment: Improve ventilation, reduce humidity, prune lower leaves and avoid overhead irrigation.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.prevention: Use resistant varieties, greenhouse ventilation, wider spacing and sanitation.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.source: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines - Tomato

Tomato_Septoria_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Many small circular spots with grey/tan centers and dark margins; lower leaves yellow and drop.
Tomato_Septoria_Leaf_Spot.cause: Fungal disease caused by Septoria lycopersici.
Tomato_Septoria_Leaf_Spot.organic_treatment: Remove infected leaves, mulch, rotate crops and avoid splashing water.
Tomato_Septoria_Leaf_Spot.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide if disease spreads.
Tomato_Septoria_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Crop rotation, sanitation, staking/pruning and drip irrigation.

Tomato_Spider_Mites_Two-spotted_Spider_M.symptoms: Fine stippling/yellow speckling, webbing on leaf undersides, bronzing and leaf drying under severe infestation.
Tomato_Spider_Mites_Two-spotted_Spider_M.organic_treatment: Spray water to reduce dust, conserve predatory mites, remove heavily infested leaves, and use neem/horticultural oils where suitable.
Tomato_Spider_Mites_Two-spotted_Spider_M.chemical_treatment: Use miticide only after confirming infestation and rotating modes of action.
Tomato_Spider_Mites_Two-spotted_Spider_M.prevention: Monitor undersides of leaves, avoid dusty dry conditions and avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum insecticides.
Tomato_Spider_Mites_Two-spotted_Spider_M.source: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines - Tomato
Tomato_Spider_Mites_Two-spotted_Spider_M.display_name: Tomato Spider Mites Two-Spotted Spider Mite

Tomato_Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots sometimes with concentric rings; lesions may coalesce and cause defoliation.
Tomato_Target_Spot.cause: Fungal disease caused by Corynespora cassiicola.
Tomato_Target_Spot.organic_treatment: Remove infected debris, improve airflow and avoid overhead irrigation.
Tomato_Target_Spot.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide if disease pressure is high.
Tomato_Target_Spot.prevention: Crop rotation, sanitation, resistant varieties where available and humidity management.
Tomato_Target_Spot.source: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines - Tomato

Tomato_Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaves, stunting, flower drop and reduced fruit set.
Tomato_Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Viral disease caused by tomato yellow leaf curl virus, transmitted mainly by whiteflies.
Tomato_Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_treatment: Rogue infected plants early and control weeds/alternate hosts.
Tomato_Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.chemical_treatment: No curative chemical treatment; manage whitefly vector with locally recommended IPM/insecticides.
Tomato_Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use virus-free seedlings, insect-proof nursery, resistant varieties, whitefly monitoring and reflective mulch/netting where feasible.
Tomato_Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.display_name: Tomato Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus

Tomato_healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Tomato_healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Tomato_healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Tomato_healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Tomato_healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Wheat_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; leaves/fruits appear normal for the crop.
Wheat_Healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good crop hygiene, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, and routine monitoring.
Wheat_Healthy.chemical_treatment: Not applicable unless a specific pest or disease is diagnosed.
Wheat_Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid water stress, and monitor regularly.
Wheat_Healthy.source: PlantwisePlus Knowledge Bank and agricultural extension references

Wheat_septoria.symptoms: Irregular tan-brown leaf lesions with tiny black pycnidia; lower leaves affected first and disease moves upward.
Wheat_septoria.cause: Fungal disease, commonly Zymoseptoria tritici or related Septoria/Stagonospora species.
Wheat_septoria.organic_treatment: Rotate crops, manage residue, use balanced fertilization and avoid overly dense canopy.
Wheat_septoria.chemical_treatment: Use recommended fungicide if disease reaches upper leaves before/around heading.
Wheat_septoria.prevention: Resistant varieties, certified seed, crop rotation, residue management and monitoring in wet weather.

Wheat_stripe_rust.symptoms: Yellow-orange powdery pustules arranged in stripes along leaves; severe infection causes yellowing and yield loss.
Wheat_stripe_rust.cause: Fungal disease caused by Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici.
Wheat_stripe_rust.organic_treatment: Use resistant varieties and remove volunteer wheat/grass hosts where practical.
Wheat_stripe_rust.chemical_treatment: Apply recommended fungicide early when rust appears on susceptible varieties.
Wheat_stripe_rust.prevention: Resistant varieties, timely sowing, monitoring during cool humid weather and avoiding volunteer hosts.
